mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an exceptionally accommodative monetary policy, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precedes economic slowdowns and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales indicates robust consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST and RSAFS both rising) fails to predict positive returns in > 60% of cases over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (as indicated by rising FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production exceeding 1.0% signals a manufacturing slowdown, which historically precedes economic weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A GDP level above 13500 billion dollars (a historical threshold for strong economic growth) signals robust economic conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 > 13500.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high employment (PAYEMS > 133000) and low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signal a strong labor market without monetary tightening, which historically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market strength without monetary tightening
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS > 133000 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) fails to predict positive returns in > 60% of cases over the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in CPI exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals accelerating inflation, which typically triggers monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 3 months.
